headline.purpose: The FlowGraph wordmark and the sign-in heading only. The two places that are not the instrument.

title.purpose: Panel headers and track-node titles. The largest type inside any working surface.

body.purpose: Controls, menu items, library rows, form inputs. The default.

label.purpose: Artist names, metadata fields, inspector values, secondary rows.

label-section.purpose: Collapsible section headers and field labels. The only uppercase in the system.

numeric.purpose: BPM, key, durations, positions, counts. Monospaced and tab-aligned because they are compared down a column.

num.purpose: BPM, key, durations, positions. Monospaced and tab-aligned, including the em dash for an unknown value.

shadows.name: drag
shadows.purpose: A node under the cursor — the only moment an element is literally in the air.

shadows.name: drag-simplified
shadows.purpose: The same drag event at low zoom, where the chip is smaller.

shadows.name: selected
shadows.purpose: A selected node sits slightly proud of its neighbours.

shadows.name: multi-selected
shadows.purpose: A group member — lifted, but less than the primary selection.

shadows.name: popover
shadows.purpose: Menus and select popovers, which float over everything.

motion.name: state-transition
motion.purpose: Handle opacity, scale, and border-colour on graph nodes. The system's only named duration.

motion.name: colors-default
motion.purpose: Tailwind's transition-colors default, used on every hover and active state.

motion.name: tooltip-delay
motion.purpose: Hint tooltips wait before opening and dismiss instantly.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Under prefers-reduced-motion every animation and transition is collapsed, including React Flow's pan and zoom.

density.name: default
density.purpose: The desk. The base role scale.

density.name: booth
density.purpose: One step up the same scale with the ink ramp opened up, set via data-density on the root. For reading at arm's length in a dark booth.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one committed action on a screen. The only filled accent surface in the product. Three sites exist today (sign-in submit, empty-state actions, and the top-bar Play control); Play is recorded drift, not precedent.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: var(--color-accent, #7c5cff); color: #fff; font: 500 12px/1.35 ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; padding: 8px 12px; border: none; border-radius: 6px; cursor: pointer; transition: background 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: var(--color-accent-hover, #8f73ff); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-accent, #7c5cff); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { opacity: 0.6; cursor: default; }

components.name: Outline Button
components.description: The workhorse control. Outlined over near-black; the border firms up on hover.
components.css: .ds-btn-outline { background: var(--color-surface-raised, #14141c); color: var(--color-ink-muted, #9d9dae); font: 400 11px/1.35 ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; padding: 4px 8px; border: 1px solid var(--color-border, #21212c); border-radius: 6px; cursor: pointer; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; transition: color 150ms, border-color 150ms; } .ds-btn-outline:hover { border-color: var(--color-border-strong, #2e2e3c); color: var(--color-ink, #f2f2f7); } .ds-btn-outline:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-accent, #7c5cff); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-outline:disabled { opacity: 0.4; cursor: default; }

components.name: Icon Button
components.description: 28px square. Transparent at rest, fills on hover. The active state adds a ring because the violet fill alone is ~1.3:1 and cannot survive greyscale.
components.css: .ds-icon-btn { width: 28px; height: 28px; display: grid; place-items: center; background: transparent; color: var(--color-ink-muted, #9d9dae); border: none; border-radius: 6px; cursor: pointer; transition: background 150ms, color 150ms; } .ds-icon-btn:hover { background: var(--color-surface-hover, #20202b); color: var(--color-ink, #f2f2f7); } .ds-icon-btn:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-accent, #7c5cff); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-icon-btn--active, .ds-icon-btn--active:hover { background: var(--color-accent-muted, #2a2145); color: var(--color-accent, #7c5cff); box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px rgb(124 92 255 / 0.7); }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Raised black well with a hairline border. The border itself is the focus indicator — the global ring is suppressed here.
components.html: <input class="ds-input" type="search" placeholder="Search title or artist…" aria-label="Search tracks">
components.css: .ds-input { width: 220px; background: var(--color-surface-raised, #14141c); color: var(--color-ink, #f2f2f7); font: 400 12px/1.35 ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; padding: 6px 8px; border: 1px solid var(--color-border, #21212c); border-radius: 6px; outline: none; transition: border-color 150ms; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: var(--color-ink-subtle, #6e6e80); } .ds-input:focus { border-color: var(--color-accent, #7c5cff); }

components.name: Status Pill
components.description: Fully round, 1px border, transparent fill. Tone sets border and text together. Always carries a word, never a bare colour.
components.html: SavedUnsaved#3AI
components.css: .ds-pill { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 4px; padding: 1px 6px; border: 1px solid; border-radius: 9999px; font: 500 10px/1.4 ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-pill--ok { border-color: rgb(52 211 153 / 0.4); color: var(--color-ok, #34d399); } .ds-pill--warn { border-color: rgb(251 191 36 / 0.4); color: var(--color-warn, #fbbf24); } .ds-pill--accent { border-color: rgb(124 92 255 / 0.5); color: var(--color-accent, #7c5cff); } .ds-pill--info { border-color: rgb(56 189 248 / 0.4); color: var(--color-info, #38bdf8); }

components.name: Panel
components.description: Panel black with a hairline border, 10px radius, and a fixed 40px header. Flat at rest — no shadow.

components.css: .ds-panel { width: 260px; background: var(--color-surface, #0e0e14); border: 1px solid var(--color-border, #21212c); border-radius: 10px; display: flex; flex-direction: column; overflow: hidden; } .ds-panel__head { height: 40px; flex-shrink: 0; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; gap: 8px; padding: 0 12px; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--color-border, #21212c); } .ds-panel__title { margin: 0; color: var(--color-ink, #f2f2f7); font: 500 13px/1.2 ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-panel__count { color: var(--color-ink-subtle, #6e6e80); font: 400 11px/1.2 ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, monospace; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-panel__body { padding: 12px; color: var(--color-ink-muted, #9d9dae); font: 400 12px/1.5 ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; }

components.css: .ds-node { position: relative; box-sizing: border-box; width: 240px; height: 104px; padding: 8px 10px; background: var(--color-surface-card, #191922); border: 1px solid var(--color-border, #21212c); border-radius: 8px; display: flex; flex-direction: column; justify-content: space-between; gap: 6px; transition: background 150ms, border-color 150ms; } .ds-node:hover { background: var(--color-surface-hover, #20202b); border-color: var(--color-border-strong, #2e2e3c); } .ds-node--selected, .ds-node--selected:hover { background: var(--color-surface-selected, #1e1830); border-color: var(--color-accent, #7c5cff); box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px rgb(124 92 255 / 0.6), 0 10px 15px -3px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.4); } .ds-node__setbar { position: absolute; left: 0; top: 8px; bottom: 8px; width: 3px; border-radius: 0 9999px 9999px 0; background: rgb(124 92 255 / 0.8); } .ds-node__top { display: flex; align-items: flex-start; gap: 8px; } .ds-node__art { width: 40px; height: 40px; flex-shrink: 0; border-radius: 6px; background: linear-gradient(135deg, oklch(0.52 0.15 280), oklch(0.72 0.16 320)); } .ds-node__names { min-width: 0; flex: 1; display: flex; flex-direction: column; } .ds-node__title { color: var(--color-ink, #f2f2f7); font: 500 13px/1.2 ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-node__artist { color: var(--color-ink-muted, #9d9dae); font: 400 11px/1.2 ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-node__meta { flex-shrink: 0; display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: flex-end; gap: 2px; font: 400 12px/1.2 ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, monospace; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-node__bpm { color: var(--color-bpm, #6ea8fe); } .ds-node__key { color: var(--color-key, #f472b6); } .ds-node__foot { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; height: 14px; }

components.name: Energy Dots
components.description: The clearest expression of the no-colour-alone law: the dot count is the signal and the hue on the ramp reinforces it. Announced as "Energy 4 of 5".
components.css: .ds-energy { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 3px; } .ds-energy__dot { width: 6px; height: 6px; border-radius: 9999px; background: var(--color-border-strong, #2e2e3c); } .ds-energy__dot--2 { background: var(--color-energy-2, #4ade80); } .ds-energy__dot--5 { background: var(--color-energy-5, #fb7185); }

components.name: View Switcher
components.description: Segmented control in a raised well. Every option shows its label, so the active one is marked by fill plus ring plus weight — never by the label alone.
components.css: .ds-seg { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 2px; padding: 2px; background: var(--color-surface-raised, #14141c); border: 1px solid var(--color-border, #21212c); border-radius: 8px; } .ds-seg__btn { background: transparent; border: none; cursor: pointer; padding: 4px 10px; border-radius: 6px; color: var(--color-ink-muted, #9d9dae); font: 400 12px/1.35 ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; transition: color 150ms, background 150ms; } .ds-seg__btn:hover { color: var(--color-ink, #f2f2f7); } .ds-seg__btn:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-accent, #7c5cff); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-seg__btn--on, .ds-seg__btn--on:hover { background: var(--color-accent-muted, #2a2145); color: var(--color-accent, #7c5cff); font-weight: 600; box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px rgb(124 92 255 / 0.7); }

narrative.overview:
FlowGraph is a navigational chart read in low light. The graph is terrain, transitions are routes, and a set is the course plotted through them. Charts do not decorate — they encode. Every hue in this system is a legend entry with exactly one meaning, and every mark that carries information carries it at least twice, so that meaning survives a dark room, a greyscale print, and a glance stolen mid-mix.

This is an instrument, not an app. The chrome recedes and the data dominates. Nothing animates for its own sake, nothing eases in on load, and no surface asks for attention it has not earned. The interface builds trust by being predictable rather than charming: the same track reads identically in the library, on the canvas, in the timeline, and in the inspector, because a DJ recognises material by its shape and must never have to re-learn it per panel.

Density is the point, not a compromise. Body text runs at 12px, labels at 11px, section headers at 10px uppercase, and numerics are monospaced and tab-aligned because they are read down a column and compared. What holds this together is strict rhythm — a three-step radius scale, a five-step tonal surface ramp, hairline borders — rather than generous whitespace. The system earns its density by never letting two things mean the same thing in two different ways.
keyCharacteristics: Five stepped near-black surfaces carry all depth; shadow appears only when something physically lifts off the plane.
Violet is selection and nothing else. It never signals importance, quality, or category.
Functional hues form a legend: BPM, key, energy, and each transition family own one hue apiece.
Every meaning is double-encoded — count, shape, dash pattern, or label alongside the hue.
Outlined over filled: a 1px border on near-black is the default surface treatment.
Controls are quiet at rest and firm up on hover; the interface is calm until reached for.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Violet means selection. It does not mean important, primary, recommended, new, or on-brand. If a surface needs emphasis and is not selected, it gets a border weight or an ink step — not the accent.

rules.name: The Legend Rule
rules.body: Every functional hue is an entry in a legend with exactly one referent. BPM is blue; key is rose; energy is the five-step ramp; each transition family owns its hue. Reusing a legend hue for decoration corrupts the legend for every screen at once.

rules.name: The Ring-Over-Fill Rule
rules.body: accent-muted is ~1.3:1 against the panel — too weak to carry state. Any active or selected control that fills with it must also carry a ring-accent/70 outline, because an outline is either present or absent and survives greyscale where the fill does not.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Any number a user compares against another number is monospaced and tabular-nums. BPM, key, duration, and set position are all read down a column; proportional digits make that column lie.

rules.name: The Ceiling Rule
rules.body: No working surface uses type above 13px. The 18–20px headline exists only for the wordmark and the sign-in screen — the two places that are not the instrument.

rules.name: The Viewport Rule
rules.body: The document never scrolls. If content overflows, the owning panel scrolls — never the page, never the body.

rules.name: The Fixed-Node Rule
rules.body: Graph nodes have fixed dimensions. A node whose height depends on how many badges it happens to carry makes edge anchors drift as data changes.

rules.name: The Grounded Rule
rules.body: Anything at rest casts nothing. A shadow on a static panel is a claim that it is floating, and it isn't.

rules.name: The Ten-Pixel Ceiling
rules.body: Nothing rounds past 10px. Oversized panel rounding is what makes an instrument look like a consumer app.

rules.name: The Token Rule
rules.body: No literal font size. Every size is a --text-* role. A literal is invisible to the density mode and drifts from the role it was meant to match.

rules.name: The Text-Fill Rule
rules.body: accent is a fill, a border and a ring; accent-text is the accent as text; accent-strong is the accent under white text. One hex cannot clear 4.5:1 in all three jobs.

dos: Do reserve Signal Violet (#7c5cff) for selection and set membership. Everything else earns emphasis through border weight or an ink step.
Do pair every functional hue with a second cue — a count, a shape, a dash pattern, or a written label.
Do add a ring-accent/70 outline whenever accent-muted fills an active control. The fill is ~1.3:1 and cannot carry state alone.
Do keep radii on the three-step scale: 6px controls, 8px cards, 10px panels.
Do monospace and tabular-nums every number a user compares against another number.
Do render absence honestly — an em dash, an unfilled control, or no mark at all. Never a zero standing in for unknown.
Do let panels own their overflow. The document never scrolls.
Do keep alternative routes visible at reduced weight rather than hiding them.
donts: Don't nest shells. A panel inside a panel inside a rounded rectangle is what made the previous build read as boxed; use the flush variant where surfaces meet the grid.
Don't round past 10px. No 16px cards, no pill-shaped containers.
Don't encode any meaning by colour alone — not transition type, not energy, not save state, not file availability.
Don't add decorative motion. Transitions are ~120ms and touch colour, opacity, and transform only. Nothing eases in on load, and nothing animates to attract attention.
Don't put a shadow on anything at rest. Shadow is reserved for elements genuinely lifted off the plane.
Don't introduce type above 13px inside a working surface.
Don't reuse a legend hue (BPM blue, key rose, an energy step, a technique family) for decoration — it corrupts the legend everywhere at once.
Don't invent a saturated fill for a selected row. Selection is a violet tint; a selected row must still read as a row.
